reasons: The cited text (Section 7.6) plainly imposes USD 25,000/day 'agreed liquidated damages' payable by Customer to Vendor, which is a direct hit on rule LD (flag only when Customer pays); direction and status (deviation) are correct.

The redline deletes the entire clause, which is exactly the playbook's preferred position and the smallest edit that reaches it — no cap or carve-out would satisfy 'no liquidated damages payable by Customer', and the clause has no severable Vendor-favourable content worth preserving.

The comment accurately states what was removed and why, cites the playbook position, and offers the sanctioned fallback (early-termination fee capped at three months' fees) without lecturing; tone and prefix conform.

Severity 'high' is appropriate: the amount is uncapped in the aggregate and triggered by an undefined 'dependency' delay, so it could plausibly exceed remaining contract value (walk-away territory), but the deletion remedy keeps this a negotiable high rather than critical.
Deterministic check passes and the high changed-character ratio is expected and justified for a full-clause deletion mandated by the rule.
